title: Abatement log leads
summary: Counts from an agency's released encampment abatement logs: how many hours passed between a notice being posted and the abatement at the same place.

sections.heading: What it shows
paragraphs: Agencies release two kinds of log in response to records requests: notices posted (a time and a place) and abatements completed (a time and a place). When both are imported as tables, the app matches them on the same recorded address and the same coordinates.

Hours are counted only at places with exactly one notice and exactly one abatement, so a notice is never paired with another notice's abatement. The lead gives how many were completed within 3 hours, within 24 hours, from 24 to 72 hours and later, how many are recorded completed before the notice was posted, and how many abatements dated within the notice log's period are at a place with no notice in that log.

sections.heading: Reports around an abatement
paragraphs: When a log of completed abatements is imported beside the City's Encampment reports with coordinates, the app counts the reports filed within 150 metres of each abatement, and in the ring from 150 to 800 metres around it, in the 14 days before and the 14 days after. Abatements are counted once per place and day, and only where the imported reports are complete for the whole four weeks.

For abatements with at least 10 reports in the ring beforehand, the lead also says how many had more reports there afterwards and how many fewer, and how many rose by half or more or fell by a third or more.

These are counts of report and abatement pairs, so a report near several abatements is counted once for each. A report is a resident's complaint, not a person or a camp. An abatement is often scheduled because reports were filed, so more reports before than after is expected whatever the abatement did, and the counts do not show where anyone went.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: That too little notice was given. The logs do not record which notice period applied, and 24 and 72 hours are yardsticks, not the agency's stated requirement. Notice can be given by a route the posting log does not record, and two rows at one place can be different events.
Whether anyone was present, or what was done with belongings. Neither log records it.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is not assessed: the finding restates recorded times and infers nothing to score. A notice document compared with the agency's own stated minimum is a different finding kind.
